title: How to decode a VIN, position by position
desc: What each of the 17 characters in a US VIN means, according to the federal regulation that defines it.

title: The pre-purchase inspection: what it covers and how to arrange one
desc: An independent mechanic's inspection is the most thorough check before buying. What it includes, what to ask for, and how to handle a seller who resists.

title: Open recalls on used cars: who fixes them and what they cost
desc: Used cars often carry recalls nobody acted on. Recall repairs are free — here is how to find open ones and get them done.

title: Title jumping: when the seller isn't on the title
desc: If the name on the title isn't the person selling you the car, you may not be able to register it. What 'open titles' mean for a buyer.

title: Curbstoning: when a 'private seller' is really an unlicensed dealer
desc: Some private sellers are unlicensed dealers avoiding the rules that come with a licence. How to recognise one and why it matters.

title: The VIN check digit: how to tell if a VIN is valid
desc: Position 9 of a US VIN is calculated from the other 16. How the calculation works, and what a failed check means.

title: VIN cloning: how it works and how to catch it
desc: A cloned VIN is a real number copied from a legitimate car. It passes every quick check. Here is what catches it.

title: Dealer or private seller: what changes for the buyer
desc: The same used car carries different protections depending on who sells it. What you gain and lose with a dealer versus a private party.

title: Buying a used car in another state
desc: Crossing a state line adds title, registration, tax and inspection steps. What to sort out before you pay.

title: The used-car test drive: what to actually check
desc: A test drive is an inspection, not a joyride. What to check before starting, while driving, and after you stop.

title: Signs of frame or structural damage
desc: Structural damage decides whether a car protects you in the next crash. What to look for, and why a repair isn't automatically bad.

title: You bought the car and found a problem. What now?
desc: A hidden defect, an undisclosed accident, a title brand you missed. What to gather, who to contact, and in what order.

title: Before you travel to buy a car
desc: A flight or a long drive to collect a car is money spent before you know the car is right. What to confirm before you leave.

title: Buying a car from an estate
desc: A car sold after its owner has died is often well kept and well priced. The complication is almost always the title.

title: Deposits and holds: when paying early is safe and when it isn't
desc: Sellers ask for deposits to hold a car. Some requests are routine; others are the start of a scam. How to tell them apart.

title: Ex-rental and ex-fleet cars: what their history shows
desc: Former rental and company cars are common on used lots. What that history means for condition, and how to find it.

title: Checking a used motorcycle's history
desc: Motorcycles carry VINs and title records like cars, but the risks and the dealer disclosures differ. What to check.

title: Checking a used RV's history
desc: A motorhome is a vehicle and a building. What the VIN check covers, what it misses, and where water damage hides.

title: Boats don't have a VIN: checking a Hull Identification Number
desc: Boats carry a 12-character HIN instead of a VIN. What the characters mean, where it must be, and what a tampered one looks like.

title: Buying an imported or grey-market vehicle
desc: A vehicle not originally built for the US market has to clear federal safety and emissions rules. What that means for a buyer.

title: What 'certified pre-owned' actually means
desc: The label sounds official. It can mean a manufacturer-backed program or a dealer's own marketing. How to tell which one you're getting.

title: Buying a car with a duplicate title
desc: Titles get lost and replaced all the time. A duplicate can also hide a lien. How to tell a routine replacement from a problem.

title: What a used-car bill of sale should include
desc: A bill of sale is your record of what was agreed. What to put in it, and why the VIN and the words 'as is' matter.

title: Hail-damaged cars: when a total loss is only skin deep
desc: Hail can total a car without touching its mechanics. What that means for the title, the price, and the inspection.

title: Fire-damaged cars: what to look for
desc: Fire and heat damage can be cleaned up cosmetically while leaving wiring, seals and structure compromised. How to spot it.

title: Airbag deployment history: what to check
desc: If the airbags have deployed, the car has been in a significant crash. How to find out, and what to confirm about the replacement.

title: Buying a car that was stolen and recovered
desc: A recovered theft vehicle can be sold legally. What the record shows, how to confirm the theft report is cleared, and what to inspect.

title: Former police, taxi and rideshare cars
desc: Hard-working former service vehicles reach the used market regularly. How their use shows up and what it does to the car.

title: Does the factory warranty transfer to a used-car buyer?
desc: Many new-car warranties continue with the vehicle, but terms differ by manufacturer and by type of coverage. How to find out what's left.

title: State inspection and emissions records: what they reveal
desc: Where states require vehicle inspections, the records they create can confirm mileage and reveal problems. How to use them.

title: Buying a used car in California: salvage, revived salvage and smog
desc: California separates salvage cars that can return to the road from non-repairable ones that never can. What each record means, and what the seller owes you on smog.

title: Buying a used car in Texas: salvage, nonrepairable and rebuilt salvage titles
desc: Texas draws a hard line between salvage cars that can be rebuilt and nonrepairable ones that cannot. And since 2025 most cars no longer get a state safety inspection before registration.

title: Buying a used car in Florida: rebuilt, flood and certificate-of-destruction vehicles
desc: Florida law makes sellers disclose rebuilt and flood status in writing, plus past use as a taxi, police car or short-term rental. What the brands mean and which papers end a car's road life.

title: Buying a used car in New York: the rebuilt salvage brand, the salvage exam and the used car lemon law
desc: New York brands rebuilt salvage titles only on vehicles up to 8 model years old. What that means for older cars, what the DMV salvage exam checks, and when the used car lemon law protects you.

title: Buying a used car in Pennsylvania: reconstructed, flood and recovered-theft titles
desc: Pennsylvania brands rebuilt cars as reconstructed, flood or recovered theft, and requires a one-time enhanced inspection. Why some theft recoveries carry no brand at all.

title: Buying a used car in Illinois: salvage certificates, REBUILT titles and the rebuilt disclosure
desc: In Illinois, a salvage certificate can only be assigned to licensed businesses, rebuilt cars get a REBUILT title, and sellers must hand over a rebuilt-status disclosure. What that means for a private buyer.

title: Buying a used car in Ohio: rebuilt salvage titles and the Highway Patrol inspection
desc: Ohio lets anyone buy a salvage car, then requires a Highway Patrol inspection and a REBUILT SALVAGE title before it goes back on the road. What the inspection paperwork can tell you.

title: Buying a used car in Georgia: salvage and rebuilt titles, older cars and emissions
desc: Georgia treats out-of-state flood, fire and water brands as salvage, inspects rebuilt cars before repairs begin, and doesn't require titles on its oldest vehicles. What that means for a buyer.

title: Buying a used car in North Carolina: the damage disclosure statement and title brands
desc: North Carolina sellers must answer five damage questions in writing before a sale, and total-loss cars get a doorjamb marker. How to read the disclosure and the title.

title: Buying a used car in New Jersey: the used car lemon law, flood titles and salvage
desc: New Jersey requires dealers to give a written warranty on many used cars, with clear exceptions. How the lemon law works, how flood vehicles are marked, and what salvage restoration involves.
